concept.conceptName: Tittle: the dot that fell off the i
concept.pitch: One amber dot falls off the i in "Liu" and lives through each project. It becomes a 16-byte ticket waiting in a Redis queue, then pure noise that 200 denoising steps turn into a brain slice, then a 5 Hz telemetry ping, then a game that Alex's own Windows service kills on sight. Every animation is the real algorithm at toy scale: FIFO lists with an 8-or-200 ms batch rule, the DDIM √ᾱ path, range and rate alert rules, and a WMI kill. An engineer who looks closely finds it correct, and the footnotes admit what has not been measured yet. Recruiters will remember "the dot site", and engineers will remember that it was honest.
concept.firstFiveSeconds: 0.0 s: Real DOM text paints immediately. "Alex Liu" is set in Bricolage Grotesque 800 at clamp(4.5rem, 14vw, 11rem), with the school line and the lede under it. LCP is text, and there is no loader. With JS on, the h1's color turns transparent in the same frame the canvas starts drawing (the text is still selectable and read by screen readers), so nothing pops. 0.0 to 0.6 s: about 1,750 bone-colored dots fade in, scattered over the right two-thirds of the viewport and drifting in a slow pseudo-curl field like dust in a projector beam. 0.6 to 1.8 s: they spring onto glyph pixels sampled from the h1's real bounding box. Per-particle stiffness jitter of ±30% makes this read as a ripple rather than a wipe. The last 48 dots, in amber, gather into the dot over the i in "Liu" and glow softly (dark mode). 1.8 to 2.4 s: the school line ("B.S.E. Computer Science · University of Michigan College of Engineering · expected May 2028") and the lede rise 8 px and fade in with the 600 ms settle ease. 2.6 s: the amber dot blinks (squashes to 20% height for 110 ms), hops 6 px, then leans toward the cursor. Moving the mouse through the letters parts them like grass, and they spring back with a slight overshoot. 3.5 s: three amber dots trickle down from under the name toward a small mono cue, "follow the dot", and loop. By 5 s the visitor has seen a name, Michigan CS with a 2028 graduation, one sentence about what he builds, and a small creature that clearly wants to go somewhere.
narrative: HERO: name and school. Tone: plain and confident, no greeting. The h1 is "Alex Liu". The school line reads "B.S.E. Computer Science · University of Michigan College of Engineering · expected May 2028". The lede reads "I build the systems around models: training them on a GPU cluster, serving them through a queue, and checking whether my own numbers hold up." A Now line reads "Now: BIM/VDC development intern at Miller Industries · software engineering researcher in the SOCR lab · Director of Infrastructure for CLAWS, a NASA SUITS team." A mono links row has GitHub · LinkedIn · Résumé (PDF) · liualex639@gmail.com. The cue reads "follow the dot".

BRIDGE: the dot leaves. As the visitor scrolls, the amber tittle lifts off the i. The particle name now reads "Lıu" (dotless), a quiet joke that nobody has to explain. The letters shed into a comet tail behind the dot, and it falls into the first project. No copy, only motion. The site's sticky mini-index (01 to 05, right edge) lights its first marker.

01 INFERENCE SERVER. Tone: a request's life story, told in protocol verbs. Dek: "An image goes in. A 16-byte ticket waits in Redis. A worker grabs up to eight tickets, runs them through ResNet-18 in one pass, and sends back 24 bytes each." There are eight flow beats in mono (POST / → park on a Future → SET + RPUSH jobs → BLPOP, batch window → MGET + DEL → one forward pass → pack '<16sq', RPUSH response → reader wakes the Future). Footnote in the confessional voice: "No speedup chart yet. The same unbatched code measured about 2× apart on two different days, so batching gets a controlled rerun before it gets a number." Known limits, one line: "A request whose image fails to decode waits forever (the Future has no timeout), and one shared response list means one frontend process."

02 SOCR BRAINGEN. Tone: careful, research-grade, generous with credit. Dek: "Pick a lobe and a size. The tumor is drawn first, as a mask. Then 200 denoising steps paint a synthetic FLAIR slice around it, in about 10 seconds on Hugging Face ZeroGPU." Credit line: "The lab's web app and GAN models came before me. I added the diffusion model, its GPU backend, and the evaluation harness. Advisors: Profs. Ivo Dinov and Simeone Marino. Manuscript in preparation." Figure caption: "fig. 02, illustration. Procedural slice, not patient data. With η = 0 and a perfect noise estimate, DDIM's path is exactly x_t = √ᾱ_t·x₀ + √(1−ᾱ_t)·ε, which is what the dots are doing."

03 CLAWS TELEMETRY. Tone: mission control, terse. Dek: "Two astronauts, 22 suit readings each, checked on every update. Out of range turns red, off nominal turns amber, changing too fast gets flagged, and the worst problem sorts to the top." Credit: "Teammates built the Flask/Socket.IO backend and the Unity telemetry client. The EVA screen and its alert rules are mine, and so is the onboarding simulator new members learn on." Honest caption: "The team's live feed refreshes each stream about every 6 s. The 5 Hz pings here come from the onboarding mock."

04 NOVERWATCH. Tone: self-deprecating and deadpan, the comic relief right before the serious experience list. Dek: "I wrote a Windows service to keep me off Overwatch. It doesn't stop the game from launching. It waits for Windows to announce the process, then kills it." Pull line in display type: "The game launches. Then it doesn't." Stats in mono: "8 kills logged in testing · March 2026 · 8 different PIDs". Asides: "42 publishes, 14 of them failed. Then it worked." and "89.5 MB, self-contained, to close one game." A 'What I'd fix' list confesses the watcher leak, the log-level gate, and the per-watcher counter. Note: "Not public. Happy to walk through the source."

MORE WORK (generic scenes, data-driven). Tone: compact. MapReduce: "Manager/worker MapReduce over raw TCP and HTTP across six worker processes. Heartbeats catch silent workers, and tasks are reassigned within about one to two seconds under injected faults, with no finished work lost." Systems & algorithms: "MST plus approximate and optimal TSP over 10,000-node graphs in C++. A cycle-accurate five-stage MIPS pipeline simulator in C, with forwarding and hazard detection." Described only, no code links.

EXPERIENCE. Tone: résumé-dense but readable, with dates in mono. Miller Industries (Sept. 2026 to present), SOCR (Dec. 2025 to present), Field AI (Mar. to July 2026), CLAWS (Mar. 2026 to present). Each entry gets one or two bullets taken only from repo-consistent facts. A skills line follows in mono. The dot rests in the margin as a living bullet beside whichever row is hovered or focused.

FOOTER: home. The heading reads "Say hı" (aria-label "Say hi"), and the dot flies back to land as the tittle of that i with a small squash. Below it are the email, GitHub, LinkedIn, and résumé. Fine print in mono: "Plain HTML, CSS and JS. No build step. 1,750 dots, one of them amber."
concept.character: Tittle, the dot over the i in "Liu", leaves home and turns into whatever each project needs. It is made of two kinds of particles in one pool. The CORE is 48 amber particles at 2.6 px. In dark mode a single pre-rendered 64 px radial-gradient sprite is drawn at the core's centroid with 'lighter' compositing. In light mode there is no glow, only solid darker amber. The BODY is 1,700 bone or ink particles on desktop (750 on phones), drawn as 1.6 to 2.2 px squares. Spare particles become DUST, drifting across the viewport at 8% alpha. Everything is drawn on one fixed full-viewport <canvas> (2D context, DPR capped at 2, or 1.5 on phones) with pointer-events none, so text stays selectable. Particle state lives in structure-of-arrays Float32Arrays: x, y, vx, vy, tx, ty, plus k (per-particle stiffness jitter 0.7 to 1.3), mode (0 spring, 1 ballistic, 2 dust), colorIndex (Uint8 into an 8-entry palette read from CSS tokens), and alpha. Motion uses a damped spring toward the target, with k = 140 s⁻² × jitter and damping ratio 0.8 (about 1.5% overshoot, organic). A pseudo-curl drift (sin/cos of position and time, not full simplex) is added, and its amplitude, from 0 to 36 px/s², is set per scene state. dt is clamped to 1/30 s so iOS low-power 30 fps still settles correctly. Drawing batches by color: one beginPath, n rect() calls, one fill() per palette entry. The core has five behaviors. Idle: it breathes, radius 9 px ±4% at 0.25 Hz. Blink: every 4 to 9 s at random, scaleY 0.2 for 110 ms. Lean: it moves up to 6 px toward the pointer. Startle: if scroll velocity goes above 4,000 px/s, body particles draw as short streaks along their velocity while the core holds still. Travel: during a section change the body trails the core with lag proportional to particle index, like a comet. A scene can take over core particles by index: 16 of them become the job id, 8 the class index, or they become the lesion seed, the TSS ping source, or the 'Play' cursor.

scenes.project: Hero: Alex Liu, University of Michigan
scenes.form: The glyphs of 'Alex Liu' are stippled by the body particles, sampled from the h1's actual bounding box in the actual font after document.fonts.load('800 1em Bricolage Grotesque'). The 48-particle amber core sits exactly where the dot over the i would be. Unused particles drift as dust.
scenes.scrollChoreography: The section is 160vh with a 100vh sticky inner. p 0 to 0.30: letters breathe and drift amplitude rises from 0 to 10 px/s². p 0.30 to 0.55: the core lifts off the i on an arc (up 40 px, then falling right), leaving 'Lıu'. Letters shed starting from the top-right of the final 'u'; each shed particle's target becomes a slot in a comet tail behind the core. p 0.55 to 0.85: the core falls down the right edge of the stage toward the Inference client anchor while body particles stream behind it. Leftover letter particles change to dust mode at alpha 0.08. p 0.85 to 1: hand-off, and the Inference scene owns the whole pool. Every target is a pure function of p, so scrolling back rebuilds the name and the dot hurries home, landing with a 90 ms squash. The top bar (name and nav) fades in for p > 0.6.
scenes.clickHoverReactions: Pointer within 90 px pushes body particles away (force ∝ (1 − d/90)², capped at 900 px/s²), and they spring back with overshoot. The core leans toward the pointer and blinks twice as often while the pointer is close. Clicking the core makes it hop 14 px and land with a squash (scaleY 0.7 for 90 ms). Clicking letters sends a ripple ring out from the click point (radius grows at 600 px/s, 12 px displacement decaying over 0.5 s). On touch, a tap makes the ripple and there is no hover repel. Idle for 12 s: the core hops twice toward the 'follow the dot' cue.
scenes.contentLayout: Desktop uses a 12-column grid with 32 px gutters. The name sits on a baseline at about 38vh and spans the full width. School line, lede, and Now line sit in columns 1 to 6 in Source Serif 4 at 1.25rem. The links row is in JetBrains Mono at 0.8125rem. The 'follow the dot' cue is bottom-right. A skip link reading 'Skip to projects' is the first focusable element, and a top-bar link reads 'Just the résumé'. Mobile: the name is set at 18vw, lines stack, the gutter is 16 px, the pool has 750 particles, and the cue is centered.

scenes.form: A request packet splits into a 4×4 chip of 16 particles (the uuid4 job id, 16 bytes) and a hollow 32-particle ring (the asyncio Future). The 'image' is a 14×14 block of grey-jittered body particles. Redis appears as a key/value cloud plus two FIFO rails, 'jobs' (top) and 'response' (bottom). Four worker lanes each hold an 8-slot batch tray with a 24-particle ring timer for the 200 ms deadline. ResNet-18 is drawn as five bars whose height shrinks 224→112→56→28→14→7 while their thickness grows from 64 to 512 channels. The reply is a 3×8 block of 24 particles: 16 teal (id) and 8 amber (int64 class index), labeled struct '<16sq'. Stage coordinates below are fractions of the stage rect.
scenes.scrollChoreography: The section is 360vh with eight beats tied to the eight flow <li> elements. Default thresholds are listed; real ones come from each li's position. b1, 0.00 to 0.12, POST /: the core lands at the client anchor (0.08, 0.45). 196 body particles form the image block beside it. Seven dim ghost clients stack at the left edge (other concurrent requests). b2, 0.12 to 0.22, parked: 16 core particles snap into the id chip (label 'job_id · 16 B'). The other 32 form the Future ring, which pulses at 0.5 Hz, with labels 'await future' and 'event loop free'. b3, 0.22 to 0.34, SET + RPUSH: the image block arcs to the KV cloud at (0.38, 0.14), labeled 'SET job_id → bytes'. The id chip slides onto the tail of the 'jobs' rail (y 0.34, x 0.24 to 0.56). The ghost clients RPUSH seven more chips behind it with a 60 ms stagger, so the queue holds 8. b4, 0.34 to 0.48, BLPOP and the batch window: worker lanes at y 0.18/0.34/0.50/0.66 (x 0.62 to 0.94) light up. Our chip pops from the head into worker A's slot 1 and starts A's ring timer, drawn clockwise and mapped to 200 ms of beat time. The other seven fill A to 8 of 8 before the ring finishes, and a lid line of particles snaps shut with the label 'closed: full (8)'. In parallel, worker B takes two late ghost chips, its ring finishes first, and it shows 'closed: 200 ms (2)', so both close conditions appear. b5, 0.48 to 0.58, MGET + DEL: one braided stream carries all 8 image blocks from the cloud into tray A along a single arc ('MGET ×8 · one round trip'), and the cloud entries dissolve ('DEL'). b6, 0.58 to 0.72, forward pass: the blocks stack into 8 thin layers ('[8,3,224,224]'), flow through the ResNet bars under a 'torch.no_grad' label, and fan out into 8 thin rows ('[8,1000]'). One particle per row flares amber (argmax). b7, 0.72 to 0.84, pack + RPUSH: our row's flare and our 16 id particles regroup into the 3×8 reply block ('24 B'). Eight replies slide onto the response rail (y 0.72) from right to left. b8, 0.84 to 1.00, wake: the reader node at (0.14, 0.72), labeled 'response_reader · own connection · BLPOP response 1', pulls our block. The id particles fly to the Future ring, which fills solid and flashes once ('set_result'). The core reassembles, and a mono label '{"Category_Number": …}' types out above the client. For p > 0.95 the core drops toward the next section.
scenes.clickHoverReactions: Clicking the stage or the 'Send a request' button starts a real-time mini-run at 1/6 speed, labeled '6× slower than real'. A new client fires a new chip. Clicks inside the open window add chips to the same tray: eight inside the window close it as full, otherwise the ring closes it at the deadline (200 ms, shown as 1.2 s). aria-live (polite) announces 'Batch closed: 8 of 8, full' or 'Batch closed: 3 of 8, 200 ms deadline'. Hovering a worker lane brightens it and shows 'torch.set_num_threads(1): one thread per worker'. Hovering the jobs rail shows 'FIFO: RPUSH at the tail, BLPOP at the head'. Hovering the Future ring shows 'pending_jobs[id]: matched without polling'. Hovering the reader shows 'separate Redis connection from the request pool'. The 'Replay the 5-second bug' button switches the reader label to 'BLPOP response 0 (unbounded)' and starts a 5 s countdown labeled 'redis-py default socket timeout'. At zero, the reader silently greys out and sinks with no log line. Replies pile up on the response rail and parked Futures pulse forever, with the caption 'No error. No log. Just a hang.' After 2 s the fix plays: the reader respawns on 'BLPOP response 1', ticking once per second, and a done-callback line prints 'reader task exited: <exception>'. Caption: 'Bounded pop, plus a callback so a dying task can't die quietly.' Every interaction also has a real <button>.
scenes.contentLayout: The left column (columns 1 to 5, max 34rem) holds the kicker '01 · personal project · 2026', the h2, and the dek. Then comes the flow <ol> (8 li in JetBrains Mono, 22vh apart on desktop); the active li gets aria-current='step', a 2 px amber left rule, and weight 600. Then 'What I built' with five bullets: frontend/worker split over Redis; Futures keyed by 16-byte ids, no polling; the 24-byte '<16sq' reply; batching at 8 or 200 ms with MGET/DEL and one stacked pass; the 5 s socket-timeout diagnosis; and a load tester covering 10 to 1,200 concurrent with a 30 s read timeout so slow requests are counted instead of silently dropped. Then the footnote about not publishing numbers, the known-limits line, the stack in mono, and the GitHub link (only after the README fix). The right column (columns 6 to 12) has a sticky 100vh stage with crop-mark corners, a 'fig. 01' label, a 24 px dot grid, DOM labels positioned in percentages, and a controls row at the bottom left. Mobile: the stage is sticky at 52svh on top with a vertical layout (client top-left, rails across the middle, workers as a 2×2 grid at the bottom), and labels shrink to op names only.

scenes.form: A square plate holds a procedural axial brain slice: a hand-authored SVG path drawn through Path2D into an offscreen 256×256 canvas with three grey levels (cortex, white matter, dark ventricles), then sampled to about 1,700 points, each with a luminance. It is never patient data. Four hand-drawn lobe polygons (frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital) act as the toy atlas. The lesion is grown with the same recipe as synth_mask: a seed inside the lobe, then score = lobe weight × Gaussian compactness × smoothed value noise, and the top-N points by score. N = area fraction × lobe points (small 5 to 12%, moderate 15 to 35%, large 40 to 60%). The top 30% become the enhancing core and the rest edema. Each particle keeps a fixed Gaussian ε from a seeded mulberry32 + Box-Muller generator.
scenes.scrollChoreography: The section is 360vh with seven beats; the denoise beat gets double spacing. b1, 0.00 to 0.10, choose: the core arrives, and a parameter strip of DOM chips appears under the plate: Lobe (4), Size (S/M/L), and the level fixed at 'Middle', with the caption 'the real panel greys out the 7 of 18 lobe × level combos the data can't support'. b2, 0.10 to 0.20, pick anatomy: body particles form a ghost slice at 20% alpha in cool grey (label 'T1 from a held-out conditioning bank'), and the four lobes tint one after another (label '+ lobe probability maps'). b3, 0.20 to 0.30, draw the tumor: core particles take the lesion color, seed one point in the chosen lobe, and grow by score rank to the target area, with the core-vs-edema split appearing (label 'the mask is drawn first; it's an input, not a prediction'). A conditioning stack label locks on: 'cond [T1, mask, 6 lobes] · 1×8×256×256'. b4, 0.30 to 0.36, start from noise: every slice particle springs to its noisy position, the counter shows 't = 995 · step 1/200 · seed 4817' (illustrative seed), and the label reads 'x ~ N(0, I) · 1×1×256×256'. b5, 0.36 to 0.86, denoise ×200: scroll is quantized to t = 995, 990, …, 5, 0. Each particle's target is √ᾱ_t·x₀ + √(1−ᾱ_t)·ε, using ᾱ from the standard linear β schedule (1e-4 to 0.02 over 1,000 steps, labeled as illustrative). Luminance is mixed with the same weights. The label 'U-Net · 85,261,185 params · predicts ε' ticks on every step. The brain sharpens out of static, with a bright lesion where the mask is. b6, 0.86 to 0.94, decode: at t = 0, a 'clip [−1,1] → [0,1]' label appears and the image is crisp. b7, 0.94 to 1.00, view: DOM tabs 'FLAIR' and 'Tumor Mask' appear; the caption reads '≈10 s end to end on Hugging Face ZeroGPU (≈6.3 s of it on the GPU)', and the core leaves.
scenes.clickHoverReactions: Hovering a lobe chip makes that lobe's particles brighten by 40%. Clicking a lobe or size chip re-grows the mask in place with a 700 ms spring. Hovering the plate while it is noisy opens a denoising lens: particles whose targets fall within 80 px of the cursor snap to x₀, so the visitor can peek at the clean image. The 'Reseed' button rolls a new seed, which re-rolls both ε and the lesion placement, matching the real code where one integer seed drives both the mask randomness and the starting noise; the caption says so. The FLAIR/Tumor Mask tabs re-target particles to the mask view (black background, edema mid-grey, core white) with a 500 ms crossfade. A small text toggle, 'What a non-strict load looks like', turns the slice into a brain-shaped blob with no lesion and a muddy texture. Caption: 'A mismatched checkpoint loaded non-strictly still makes something brain-shaped. That's the scary part, so mine loads strict=True and checks the parameter count.' Everything is keyboard reachable.
scenes.contentLayout: The left column holds the kicker '02 · research · SOCR lab, University of Michigan · 2026', the h2, and the dek. Then the 7-step flow <ol>. Then 'What I built': the sixth model in the lab app (about 8.2k lines on a feature branch, UI that never silently substitutes a combo); a ZeroGPU backend where five GANs run on CPU and only the diffusion loop goes to the GPU; the strict load plus parameter check; an atlas-conforming tumor generator that matches the original SciPy version on 78 test cases (Dice 1.0); the pipeline (ANTs SyN atlas registration, about 1,250 BraTS 2023 patients turned into 163,974 nine-channel slices, mixed-precision + EMA training on Great Lakes); and an evaluation harness for all 8 lab checkpoints with 1,000-resample bootstrap CIs, audited against 27 candidate measurement defects with 5 fixed. Then 'Explored': CLIP cross-attention text conditioning and 64³ 3D diffusion, labeled as experiments. Then the credit line, the stack in mono, and the link 'Feature branch (not yet merged)' pointing to SOCR/Brain-Image-Generator/tree/feat/conddiff-brats-v1. The right column has a sticky stage with a square plate (min of 70vh and the column width), 'fig. 02', the t/step/seed counter in mono at the top-right, and the parameter strip and tabs as real buttons below the plate. Mobile: the plate is 46svh square with the chips in a horizontally scrollable row under it.

scenes.form: A dark sonar field. The core becomes the 'mock_tss.py' node at the left. Every 200 ms (live, not scroll-driven) a ring of 72 body particles expands from it and fades. Two astronaut markers (EVA-1, EVA-2) are 12-particle clusters walking between small cross-shaped points of interest and rotating to their heading. Further in, particles form the EVA screen: two columns of 22 thin gauge bars each, every bar about 8 particles tall, with hairline min/max bands and a nominal tick.
scenes.scrollChoreography: The section is 280vh with six beats. b1, 0.00 to 0.15, mock TSS: the core settles at (0.10, 0.5), labeled 'sim_loop · 5 Hz'. Pings begin, and the astronauts fade in on the field (right half), walking. b2, 0.15 to 0.30, WebSocket: a /ws line stretches from the node to three client glyphs in mono ('panel.py watch', 'TssClient.cs', 'pytest'), and each ping sends a small packet of 6 particles along the line. A Unity caption reads 'newest frame parked on a background thread, parsed on the main thread, marker lerps to (x, y)'. b3, 0.30 to 0.50, the EVA screen: the field slides left and shrinks to a 30% inset while body particles form the 2 × 22 gauge bars (label '22 suit fields × 2 astronauts · checked on every update'). Bars jitter slightly with each incoming frame. b4, 0.50 to 0.70, the rules: min/max bands draw in. One bar drifts off nominal and turns amber ('warn'), one crosses its min and turns red ('danger'), and one jumps faster than its rate limit and strobes softly at 1 Hz ('changing fast': |Δ|/Δt over the limit). b5, 0.70 to 0.85, sort and dedupe: a DOM alert list on the right re-orders danger first. A repeated alert pulses its existing row instead of adding a duplicate (deduped by id), and alert ids tint the matching bars. b6, 0.85 to 1.00, onboarding: the view pulls back, and four extra small client dots join the /ws line (new members on their own branches, unnamed). The label reads 'learn the whole data path on a laptop'. The core detaches and drops.
scenes.clickHoverReactions: A command-style button, 'uia o2_vent open' (mirroring panel.py and POST /uia/o2_vent {"value": true}), flips the switch glyph. On the next tick the O2 bars of both astronauts start draining. First a 'changing fast' flag appears, then the bar crosses min, turns red, and its alert sorts to the top; aria-live announces 'EVA-1 O2: below range'. Clicking again ('close') refills, and the alerts clear. Clicking an astronaut marker sends a phosphor-green ping from that astronaut. Hovering a gauge bar widens its min/max band and nominal tick (no invented values, band only). Hovering the TSS node shows 'full State JSON pushed to every /ws client each tick'. Rings are thin and at most 35% alpha, so there are no full-field flashes.
scenes.contentLayout: The left column holds the kicker '03 · CLAWS, a University of Michigan NASA SUITS team · 2026' (the acronym is never expanded), the h2 'CLAWS telemetry', the dek, and the 6-step flow <ol>. Then 'What I built': the team's EVA telemetry screen, now the live /eva route, with about 700 of its roughly 750 lines his; the client-side caution and warning engine (22 fields with min/max/nominal, 10 per-second rate limits, deduped, danger-first); a mock of NASA's Telemetry Stream Server streaming at 5 Hz over WebSockets with a CLI panel and a Unity C# client; a pytest that runs the NASA egress procedure against the sim in fast-forward; and repo setup (Git LFS rules, Node .gitignore, the first GitHub Actions workflow). Then the teammate credit line, the 6 s vs 5 Hz caption, and the link 'Onboarding repo' pointing to github.com/ALIUD1/Infra-2026-2027-onboarding. The team repo is private and gets no link. The right column has a sticky stage with 'fig. 03' and the alert list as real DOM (role='log', aria-live='polite' only after user actions). Mobile: field on top and bars below it inside the 52svh stage; the alert list collapses to the top 2 rows.

scenes.form: A big rounded 'PLAY' button made of about 900 body particles, with the mono label 'Overwatch.exe' under it. It is a generic play shape, never the game's logo or art. It becomes a window frame (title bar plus a loading bar) labeled 'Overwatch.exe · PID 12400'. A horizontal tripwire of kill-red particles represents the WMI watcher. The kill is a shatter: particles switch to ballistic mode, then gather into a debris pile. A small sentry eye made of core particles keeps a heartbeat.
scenes.scrollChoreography: The section is 240vh with five beats. b1, 0.00 to 0.18, Play: the core arrives and acts as a cursor; body particles form the PLAY button, which swells 4% as the core approaches. b2, 0.18 to 0.34, the process starts: the button depresses (scaleY 0.92), and its particles re-target into the window frame while the loading bar fills to 30%. Caption: 'Windows creates the process first. Noverwatch doesn't prevent anything.' b3, 0.34 to 0.46, the tripwire: a red line sweeps across the stage, labeled 'SELECT * FROM Win32_ProcessStartTrace'. An event particle runs along it to the window, labeled 'EventArrived: Overwatch.exe, 12400', then 'matches config["Games"]'. b4, 0.46 to 0.60, kill: at the beat midpoint every window particle switches to ballistic mode with a radial velocity of 300 to 900 px/s from the window center, plus spin jitter and 1,400 px/s² gravity, bouncing on the stage floor with 0.3 restitution. The stage shakes 4 px for 180 ms. Log lines type out in a DOM terminal: 'Overwatch PID: 12400 blocked at <visitor's local time>', then 'crit: Overwatch has been killed(stopped)!', then 'crit: Blocked 1'. Scrubbing back above the threshold springs the debris back into the window, which plays the kill in reverse. b5, 0.60 to 1.00, the sentry: after 1.2 s the debris settles into a pile, and the core reassembles as a small eye that blinks a heartbeat every 10 s ('warn: The Noverwatch system is online'; the caption says the real interval is 100 s). Stats fade in: '8 kills logged in testing · March 2026 · 8 different PIDs'. At p > 0.9 the core gets up with a limp (one frame of tilt), shakes it off, and leaves.
scenes.clickHoverReactions: The 'Launch Overwatch' button, or clicking PLAY, replays in real time: the window forms over 600 ms and the shatter follows about 400 ms later. Each run appends a fresh log line with a random PID and the visitor's own clock time, followed by 'Blocked 1'. On the third launch a footnote slides in: 'Yes, it always says 1. timesBlocked is a local in each watcher, so the count resets. It's on the fix list.' Hovering PLAY makes the particles lean eagerly toward the cursor while the red tripwire glows faintly (it's watching). Hovering the debris lets the visitor stir it around. Under reduced motion there is no shake and the window cuts to debris.

Then it doesn't.' set in display 600 at 2.25rem, and the 5-step flow <ol>. scenes.scrollChoreography: Each section is 200vh (from data-length). For p < 0.15, the body forms the glyph in Bricolage 800. From 0.15 to 0.85 the glyph breaks into N clusters, one per li, placed along a gentle S-curve across the stage. A stream of 10% of the body flows continuously from cluster i to i+1. The cluster whose li is current scales 1.4× in the accent color while the others sit at 50% ink. For p > 0.85 the clusters re-form the glyph and the core exits.
scenes.clickHoverReactions: Click or tap sends a pulse: the core runs the chain from first cluster to last in 900 ms, lighting each in turn. Hovering or focusing a flow li swells its cluster (pointerenter/focusin on the li). Hovering the stage pushes the stream gently, like the hero.

concept.genericScene: 'Constellation of steps'. Any project <article> that has no data-scene, or an unknown one, gets this scene with no new code. Inputs come from the article only: data-glyph (1 to 4 characters, defaulting to the h2's initials), data-accent (a hex value, defaulting to --dot), data-length (viewport heights, default 2), and its <ol class="flow"> items (at least 2). Choreography: for p 0 to 0.15, the body stipples the glyph in Bricolage Grotesque 800, sized to 60% of the stage height. For p 0.15 to 0.85, the glyph breaks into N sunflower-packed clusters, one per flow item (Fibonacci disc layout, body/N particles each), along an S-curve that spans the stage. About 10% of the body forms a continuous stream between consecutive clusters, with each particle's position along the curve = (time × 0.12 + its offset) mod 1. The cluster for the current li (whose center has crossed mid-viewport) scales 1.4× in the accent color while the others sit at 50% ink. For p 0.85 to 1, the clusters re-form the glyph and the core exits downward. Reactions: a click or tap sends a pulse that carries the core through every cluster in 900 ms. Hovering or focusing an li swells its cluster. Reduced motion shows the clusters at rest with the stream frozen as a dotted line, and the current cluster in accent. Because every project is a process, the result reads as 'this thing has stages' and never looks broken. Adding a project is: copy an <article>, fill in its text and flow list, and optionally set data-glyph and data-accent.
concept.visualSystem: PALETTE, as CSS custom properties on :root. The canvas reads them through getComputedStyle at boot and again on a prefers-color-scheme change. DARK ('night lab', the default look): --bg #0D0E0B (warm near-black); --bg-raised #161712; --ink #EDE8DA (bone); --ink-muted #9E9A8A (6.9:1 on bg); --rule #2B2C24; --dot #FFB13B (the familiar, amber); --dust is --ink at 8% alpha; --queue #5FD4BF (Inference teal); --flair #E9E4D4 with --lesion #FF6A3D (BrainGen); --phosphor #A6E35A, --warn #FFC94A, --danger #FF5A47 (CLAWS); --kill #FF4436 (Noverwatch). LIGHT ('paper lab'): --bg #F2EEE4; --bg-raised #E9E3D5; --ink #1A1B16; --ink-muted #5C594E (6.1:1 on bg); --rule #D3CCBB; --dot #B86E00; --queue #0E7F6E; --flair #1A1B16 (graphite stipple on paper) with --lesion #C93F18; --phosphor #4A7D12; --warn #9A6A00; --danger #B8281A; --kill #B3241A. Accent colors are for particles, rules and labels of 24 px or larger only. Body text is always ink or ink-muted. color-scheme is 'light dark', and body has an explicit background. No gradients except the core's glow sprite in dark mode. No glass, no blur, no purple. FONTS (Google Fonts, display=swap, preconnect): Bricolage Grotesque (opsz 12 to 96; weight 800 for the name and particle glyphs, 600 for h2 and pull lines); Source Serif 4 (400, 400 italic, 600; opsz 8 to 60) for body, giving an editorial, lab-paper voice; JetBrains Mono (400, 500) for flows, Redis ops, captions, log lines and dates. TYPE SCALE: name clamp(4.5rem, 14vw, 11rem) with -0.035em tracking; h2 clamp(2rem, 5vw, 3.5rem); dek 1.25rem/1.45; body 1.0625rem/1.65; mono 0.8125rem/1.5 with +0.01em tracking; kicker in mono uppercase at 0.75rem and +0.08em. Measure is 62ch. SPACING: 4 px base with steps 4/8/12/16/24/32/48/72/120. Gutters are 16 px on mobile and 32 px on desktop. Grid is 12 columns at 1100 px and up; text uses columns 1 to 5 (max 34rem) and the stage uses columns 6 to 12. Breakpoints are 768 and 1100. TEXTURE: each stage is a 'figure plate' with a 1 px dot grid every 24 px in --rule, 12 px L-shaped crop marks at the corners, and a 'fig. 0N' mono label. The body has a static SVG feTurbulence grain (3.5% opacity in dark mode, 5% multiply in light mode), which is never animated. Focus is a 2 px --dot outline with a 3 px offset. Icons: none. Mono glyphs and arrows (→) only. MOTION: DOM reveals use --ease-settle cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.1,1) over 600 ms (translateY 10px→0 plus opacity). UI toggles use --ease-snap cubic-bezier(.6,0,.2,1) over 180 ms. Exits use cubic-bezier(.7,0,.84,0) over 300 ms. Particles use a damped spring (k = 140 s⁻², damping ratio 0.8, per-particle k jitter ±30% for organic stagger), pseudo-curl drift from 0 to 36 px/s² depending on scene state, and ballistic shatter with 1,400 px/s² gravity and 0.3 restitution. Only transform and opacity are ever animated in the DOM.

concept.techPlan: FILES (no build step; ES modules served by GitHub Pages from ALIUD1/ALIUD1.github.io main at the root, plus an empty .nojekyll). index.html holds all content and is the single data file for projects. style.css holds tokens, layout, sticky story, reduced motion and no-JS rules. js/main.js (~200 lines) handles boot, reading articles into a scene list, theme tokens, the reduced-motion switch, scroll/resize/pointer/button wiring, the rAF loop, adaptive quality, and the ?check self-test. js/swarm.js (~220 lines) holds the particle pool, spring integrator, drift, batched drawing, the glow sprite, and the samplers sampleText(font, text, rect, n) and samplePath(path2dString, fills, rect, n). The samplers draw into a detached <canvas>, call getImageData, keep pixels above an alpha threshold on a stride chosen so the count is about n, and shuffle with a seeded mulberry32. js/scenes/hero.js, queue.js, denoise.js, ping.js, shatter.js and generic.js run about 120 to 250 lines each. Also favicon.svg (a single amber dot), og.png (1200×630, under 120 KB, a still of the stippled name), resume.pdf (a new, clean one), and an optional 404.html (static: 'This page isn't here. The dot checked.'). No libraries; vanilla earns its place here, and GSAP or three.js would add weight for things 300 lines of springs already do. DATA SCHEMA: each project is <article class=\"project\" id=\"slug\"> inside <section id=\"work\">. Attributes: data-scene ('queue' | 'denoise' | 'ping' | 'shatter'; absent or unknown means generic), data-accent (hex), data-glyph (1 to 4 characters, generic only), data-length (section height in viewport heights, default 2). Children: header with p.kicker and h2; p.dek; ol.flow with li items (an optional data-at gives a 0 to 1 override, otherwise the beat threshold is wherever the li's center crosses mid-viewport); ul.built; p.footnote (optional); p.stack; nav.links; div.controls of <button data-action=\"fire|reseed|lobe:frontal|size:small|vent|launch|bug|tab:mask|nonstrict\" hidden>, whose hidden attribute is removed by JS; and div.stage (aria-hidden, the hit area and the container for scene-placed labels). DOM order is page order. Adding a project means pasting one article. SCENE CONTRACT: a scene module exports setup(api, article, stageRect) returning state; update(state, p, beat, u, dt, now), which writes targets, colors and modes for the particle index ranges it owns; action(state, name); pointer(state, x, y, kind); and still(state), which writes final targets for reduced motion. main.js maps data-scene to a module and falls back to generic. A custom scene expecting K beats logs a console.warn and spaces beats evenly if the li count differs. RENDERING: one fixed full-viewport canvas with pointer-events:none, DPR capped at 2 (1.5 under 768 px). The pool is 1,750 desktop / 750 phone: indices 0 to 47 are the core and 48 onward the body, and particles not claimed by the active scene fall to dust mode. The integrator is semi-implicit Euler with dt clamped to 1/30. Drawing batches by palette index (one fill per color), plus one drawImage of the glow sprite in dark mode. When every particle is settled (max |v| < 0.02) and no live effect is running, the frame is skipped. Targets are sampled once per scene per viewport size and pre-warmed in requestIdleCallback after the hero is done. SCROLL PROGRESS: native scroll only, never hijacked. A passive scroll listener caches scrollY. Section tops and heights are cached on load and in a ResizeObserver on body. Height-only viewport changes under 120 px are ignored, which absorbs the mobile toolbar. Each frame computes p = clamp((scrollY − top) / (height − innerHeight)) for the section containing the viewport center line. The beat index and local u come from the cached li thresholds. The only layout read per frame is the active stage's getBoundingClientRect, which keeps particles glued to a sticky stage as it un-sticks. Scene hand-off happens by re-targeting; the spring stagger produces the travel. INPUT: pointer events go on .stage elements, never the canvas, converted to stage coordinates. Every canvas interaction has a real button. aria-live='polite' regions update only after user actions. PERF BUDGET: first-load transfer at most 250 KB gzipped (HTML ~25, CSS ~10, JS ~35, fonts ~140; og.png not loaded by the page). LCP is the h1 text at under 1.8 s on mid-tier mobile, CLS 0, and Lighthouse targets are 95+ performance and 100 accessibility. At most 5 ms of script per frame at 1,750 particles on an Iris Xe-class laptop. Adaptive quality: if the mean frame time over the first 90 frames is above 20 ms, halve the body (odd indices become dust) and drop the glow; if it is still above 20 ms, switch to the still path. The loop sleeps when document.hidden. Animated DOM uses transform and opacity only. REDUCED MOTION, NO JS, MOBILE: matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') is checked live. When it matches, there is no rAF loop. Each scene's still() is drawn once when its section enters (IntersectionObserver) and again on resize/theme change, with a 200 ms opacity crossfade at most. The stills: the hero is the stippled name. Inference is the full pipeline at rest (8 chips in the tray, the 24-dot reply, the filled Future). BrainGen is a triptych of three mini plates at t = 995, 500 and 0. CLAWS is three frozen rings, bars with one red alert, and the list sorted. Noverwatch is the window outline next to the debris pile, with the log lines shown. Buttons still work and just jump to their end state, and nothing shakes. No JS: <html class=\"no-js\"> is swapped by a one-line inline script in <head>. CSS hides the canvas, .stage and .controls under .no-js, and sections are height:auto, so the result is a clean editorial long-read with the mono flow lists as diagrams. Mobile (under 768 px): single column, each .stage sticky at top:0 with height 52svh on an opaque --bg, content scrolling below it, data-length × 0.8, tap acting as click, hover reactions dropped (except focus on li), the Inference stage switched to its vertical layout, and labels shortened. Local preview needs a server (python -m http.server), because modules don't load over file://. ONE CHECK: ?check in the URL runs assertions in main.js and logs failures with console.error. It checks that each article has an h2 and at least 2 flow li, that every data-scene resolves or falls back, and it runs a forbidden-phrase scan over the DOM text: '1.63', '51 req', '1.55', 'fault tolerant', 'Docker deploy', 'LPUSH', 'GPU inference', 'production', 'published' or 'submitted' near 'manuscript', 'prevents' inside #noverwatch, 'heartbeat' inside #inference-server, 'free plan', and a phone-number regex. This is the omit list written as a test.

concept.pitch: The page opens on a small coral creature called Blip, sitting where the dot on the i in "Liu" should be. As you scroll it hops off and acts out each of Alex's projects. It queues in a Redis FIFO and gets batched eight at a time. It melts into Gaussian static and denoises into a brain slice. It grows an antenna to carry spacesuit telemetry. It gets flattened by a Process.Kill() mallet the moment it launches Overwatch. Every joke runs on a real mechanism from the code (RPUSH/BLPOP, a 200 ms fill deadline, 200 DDIM steps, a WMI process-start trace), so a recruiter laughs and also leaves knowing what Alex actually built. The honesty is part of the charm: illustrations carry labels, there are "what I'd fix" cards, and no benchmark number appears until the rerun is done.
concept.firstFiveSeconds: 0.0 s: a warm paper page with a faint dot grid. "Alex Liu" is already painted huge (Bricolage Grotesque, weight 800, about 13rem). It is real, selectable text that paints first, with no wait on JS. 0.3 s: Blip drops in from above the viewport (ease-in fall, 420 ms) and lands on top of the i in "Liu", covering the dot. It squashes to 1.4x wide and 0.6x tall, bounces twice, settles and kicks up three dust specks. 1.0 s: it blinks twice, glances left at "Alex", then turns its pupils to the visitor's cursor (straight ahead on touch). 1.4 s: three lines fade up 12px with a 70 ms stagger: "Computer Science (B.S.E.), University of Michigan · Expected May 2028"; "I build ML systems and the infrastructure around them: a diffusion model for synthetic brain MRI, a batched inference server, telemetry tools for a NASA SUITS team, and the occasional robot-dog mapping run."; and a mono line, "Now: BIM/VDC development intern, Miller Industries · Researcher, SOCR lab · Director of Infrastructure, CLAWS". 2.0 s: the left rail draws top to bottom (500 ms) with numbered station ticks for each project. 3.0 s: a mono cue appears, "scroll. Blip goes first.", and Blip looks down at it. 5.0 s with no scroll: Blip leans over the edge of the i, peers down and does one impatient hop. Before the first scroll the visitor has the name, school, what he builds, current roles and the gimmick.
narrative: HERO, 'the dot' (100svh). Blip sits on the i in 'Liu'. The copy is plain and confident, with no greeting and no emoji: the h1, a school line, one sentence on what he builds, a mono 'Now:' line with current roles, and a cue: 'scroll. Blip goes first.' The tone throughout is dry and specific: first person for Alex, and mono stage directions in screenplay voice for Blip.

DESCENT (transition, about 40vh). Blip crouches (anticipation, 80 ms) and hops off the i. The font's real dot was underneath all along, so the name never looks broken. Blip lands on the left rail and slides down it like a firepole to station 01. Stage direction: 'BLIP leaves the name. It has places to be.'

01 INFERENCE SERVER, 'Blip becomes a request.' (380vh). Blip gets a 16-byte ticket and leaves its photo in a Redis key. It waits in the FIFO 'jobs' line, gets batched eight at a time and runs through ResNet-18. It rides home as a 24-byte '<16sq' message and wakes its parked request. Tone: precise and deadpan ('FIFO. No cutting.', 'ImageNet class 1 is goldfish.'). The scene ends with a 'What I'd fix next' card and a one-line note on why there are no throughput numbers yet.

02 SOCR BRAINGEN, 'Blip becomes noise.' (300vh). Blip fuzzes into Gaussian static. The visitor scrubs 200 DDIM-style steps (t = 995 to 0) into an illustrated axial brain slice, with a lesion placed by the lobe and size they picked. Tone: careful and exact, because this is medical research. Every frame is tagged as an illustration, the copy says plainly which parts are inputs and which the model makes, and a credit line names the app and GANs as the labmates' work.

03 CLAWS, 'Blip grows an antenna.' (320vh). Act A: Blip pings from NASA's Telemetry Stream Server through the team backend into Alex's /eva page, where his alert engine flags off-nominal, out-of-range and changing-fast values. Act B opens with 'Then I built a fake NASA for new teammates.': Blip pulses at 5 Hz through the onboarding mock, and the visitor can flip the O2 vent. Tone: dry mission control, with clear credit ('teammates built the backend; I built this page').

04 NOVERWATCH, 'Blip tries to play Overwatch.' (260vh). Blip puts on a headset and presses PLAY. The WMI tripwire fires, the Process.Kill() mallet comes down, and Blip ends up a pancake with X eyes. The log line is stamped with the visitor's own current time. Tone: openly self-deprecating ('I wrote a Windows service to stop myself from playing Overwatch. It works.'), then a sober 'What I'd fix' card showing he reviewed his own code.

05 ALSO BUILT, 'Blip builds it.' (generic scene, 240vh). Distributed MapReduce runs on the generic scene to prove the data system: the tech stack literally stacks up, and Blip hops across the steps. Below it is a plain list with no links: a C++ graph optimization engine (MST and TSP over 10,000-node graphs) and a cycle-accurate five-stage MIPS pipeline simulator in C.

LOGBOOK (experience, normal height). Four dated rows in a ruled ledger. Miller Industries, BIM/VDC Development Intern, Sept 2026 to present: a Python reality-capture pipeline from Autodesk Construction Cloud through ReCap Pro to RCS deliverables, and now multi-scan alignment into one shared coordinate frame. SOCR, Software Engineering Researcher, Dec 2025 to present: leads the brain image generation team under Profs. Ivo Dinov and Simeone Marino; manuscript in preparation. CLAWS, Director of Infrastructure, NASA SUITS 2026-27, Mar 2026 to present: leads a six-person infrastructure subteam. Blip sits on the edge of the ledger and reacts to whichever row is hovered.

ABOUT (one short first-person paragraph): 'I like the unglamorous parts: queues, checkpoints, CI, cloud bills (I cut one lab's by over $230 a month). I audited my own evaluation harness for 27 ways it could be lying to me; five were real, and I fixed them. I also built an offline LeetCode kit with tiered hints so flights count as practice, and a Windows service to keep me off Overwatch. You saw how that went.'

The story closes its loop: the mono line 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK' (the response has arrived), then the email liualex639@gmail.com (copy button plus mailto), GitHub ALIUD1 and LinkedIn. Blip lands at the top of the section like a returned response. Hovering the email folds Blip into an envelope, and copying it makes Blip salute and stamp 'copied'. concept.character:
Blip is a coral gumdrop creature. It is about 56px tall on desktop and 40px on phones (28px in its hero 'dot' pose), drawn in a 64x64 SVG viewBox, and it is the only saturated warm thing on the page.

BODY: one path made of 4 cubic segments (8 control points) with a flat-ish bottom and a domed top, filled --blip. A --blip-deep crescent along the bottom gives it weight, and a paper-white highlight crescent at 55% opacity sits upper-left. In dark mode a 1px --blip-cheek rim runs along the top.

FACE: two white 9x11 ellipses with ink pupils (r=4) that slide up to 2.5 units toward a look target: the cursor, the last touch point, or whatever the scene points at. Two --blip-cheek ellipses at 45% opacity. No mouth by default; a 3-unit 'o' appears only for surprise or a bonk.

SPROUT: a 2px ink stem with a 3px dot. It stretches into the CLAWS antenna.

FLOOR SHADOW: a separate ink ellipse at 12% opacity that shrinks and fades as Blip rises.

EXPRESSIONS are swapped eye shapes:
- open
- blink (scaleY 0.1 for 110 ms, every 2.5-6 s, 20% chance of a double)
- happy (^ ^ arcs)
- squint (speed)
- sleepy (half lids after 8 s idle)
- X (bonked)
- spiral (dizzy)
- offended (two 2px brows angled inward)

FORMS combine alternate body control-point sets, which JS lerps (16 numbers, same command structure, so no morph library is needed), with prop groups toggled by class:
- dot: hero, sitting on the i
- ticket: rounded 1.6:0.6 card with 32 hex chars on the belly, eyes on top
- capsule: 24 cells, 16 cobalt plus 8 green
- noise: body hidden, eyes kept
- antenna: sprout scaleY 3 with a blinking --signal tip
- ping: 0.45x ball plus 3 trail ghosts
- headset
- flat: scaleY 0.18, scaleX 1.9, orbiting stars
- envelope
- legs: 4 stubby legs with a Spot-style trot
- goggles
- hardhat: generic scene

PHYSICS:
- Position spring k=170, c=20 (damping ratio about 0.77, so a slight overshoot).
- Stretch along velocity: scaleY = clamp(1 + |v|*0.0007, 1, 1.4), scaleX = 1/scaleY (volume preserved), transform-origin at the feet.
- Landing (vy flipping from above 600 px/s) injects an impulse into a wobble spring (k=420, c=14) for two visible bounces.
- Every hop starts with a 5% crouch held 80 ms.
- Impacts get a 90 ms hit-stop.
- Squash is clamped to 0.55-1.45, except the bonk.

IMPLEMENTATION: one inline SVG inside <button aria-label='Poke Blip'>, in a fixed overlay (pointer-events: none on the overlay, auto on the button). The outer <g> takes JS transforms. The inner <g> runs CSS breathing (scale 1 to 1.02 over 2.4 s) and the blink, so idle life costs zero JS.

scenes.form: Blip becomes a request ticket. It carries a tiny photo of itself (the image payload) and gets a 16-byte job_id. Its asyncio Future appears as a reserved seat on the frontend's pending_jobs bench. It drops the photo into a Redis key (SET), then its body lerps into the ticket shape (32 hex chars on its belly, eyes on top) and it waits in the FIFO 'jobs' list. After the batched forward pass it re-forms as a 24-cell capsule ('<16sq': 16 cobalt id cells, 8 green class-index cells), rides the separate 'response' lane home to its seat and wakes the parked request.
scenes.scrollChoreography:
Section 380vh. Sticky stage: top 10vh, 80vh tall on desktop, viewBox 960x600.

Stage layout:
- client door at x40
- FastAPI frontend box (x110-300), with a 'pending_jobs' bench of Future seats and the 'response_reader' on its own 'r_reader' connection at the base
- Redis box (x330-620): a locker row of keys on top; the 'jobs' list in the middle (tail on the left labeled RPUSH, head on the right labeled BLPOP); the 'response' list along the bottom, running right to left
- 4 worker lanes W1-W4 (x650-930), each with an 8-slot batch tray, a 0.2 s ring timer and an 18-slat ResNet-18 block with skip arcs, plus a '1 torch thread' tag
- about 14 other requests as ink-outlined mini tickets with dot eyes; their positions are a pure function of p, so scrubbing is exact

Beats:
0.00-0.07: Blip runs from the rail to the client door. A 'POST /' tag pops onto its sprout and it picks up its photo.
0.07-0.15: Inside the frontend, a ticket prints a 16-byte id: 32 hex chars from crypto.getRandomValues, new each visit. A seat labeled 'Future' plus the id appears on the bench. Caption: 'Request parked on an asyncio Future. The event loop is free.'
0.15-0.24: Blip walks to the lockers and posts the photo: 'SET <job_id> <image_bytes>'. Trigger 0.21: the locker door slams with a 2-bounce wobble.
0.24-0.30: Blip squashes flat, morphs into the ticket and hops onto the tail of the list: 'RPUSH jobs <job_id>'. Trigger 0.27: plop. HUD: 'jobs: 7 · blip: QUEUED'.
0.30-0.45: Scroll is time. Idle workers pop heads ('BLPOP jobs 1') and Blip shuffles forward one slot per hop. Idle business: it taps its foot and glances at the workers. At 0.44 it is at the head.
0.45-0.56: Trigger 0.45: W3 yanks Blip, stretching toward it. The batch window opens and the ring timer starts filling. Seven more tickets join one by one ('BLPOP jobs 0.05'). Trigger 0.56: the tray hits 8, the lid claps and the ring snaps shut: 'closed: full (8)'.
0.56-0.62: 'MGET id1..id8': eight photos arc out of the lockers into the tray in one swoop. 'DEL id1..id8': the doors swing open, empty.
0.62-0.70: torch.stack turns the photos into a block labeled '[8,3,224,224]', which slides through the 18 slats under a 'torch.no_grad()' banner. Trigger 0.66: one bright pass flash. Out come 8 rows labeled '[8,1000] logits -> argmax'.
0.70-0.78: Each result packs into a 24-cell capsule. Blip becomes its capsule: 'RPUSH response <24 bytes>'.
0.78-0.88: Blip rides the bottom lane right to left with squint eyes and a trail.
0.88-0.94: The reader runs 'BLPOP response 1', unpacks and matches the id: 'set_result(1)'. Trigger 0.90: Blip pops into its seat, eyes snap open, the seat lights --ok.
0.94-1.00: Blip exits the door holding a JSON bubble: '{"Category_Number": 1, "Server_Rate": ...}'. Trigger 0.97: Blip turns to camera with offended brows next to the label 'ImageNet class 1 is goldfish.'

Scrolling back reverses everything, and triggers are undone silently.

- POKE BLIP while it's in the queue: it hops one slot forward, a 'FIFO' sign drops on its head (bonk, 90 ms hit-stop), and it shuffles back. Caption: 'FIFO. No cutting.'

concept.techPlan:
REPO AND FILES. Repo ALIUD1/ALIUD1.github.io, Pages served from main at the root, no build step, relative paths only. - index.html: the single data file. It holds the hero, the project
s between markers, the logbook, about, contact, and a commented article template. About 30 KB. - css/site.css: tokens (light and dark), layout, scrolly, rail, the .rm and .no-js rules, print. - js/main.js: boot, scroll loop, triggers, rail, theme and motion toggles, eye tracking, ?debug HUD (fps, p per scene, Blip state). - js/blip.js: Blip's SVG, springs, forms, expressions. - js/scenes/inference-server.js, braingen.js, claws.js, noverwatch.js, generic.js. - favicon.svg: Blip's face, with a dark-aware
risks: Scope: four custom scenes plus the physics is a lot for one pass. The build order is set so each step ships something usable: content first (works without JS), then Blip, the rail and the generic scene, then Noverwatch (cheapest and funniest), then Inference, CLAWS and BrainGen, then posters and mobile.

The charm can read as unserious to some ML/SWE screeners. Mitigations: the copy column is dense and factual, the hero's 'Now:' line states roles within 5 s, the rail is a real nav for skimmers, and Blip never covers text.

Resume claims that conflict with the repos are left off the site, and Alex should fix the resume to match before a recruiter compares the two. (1) It says CLAWS CI gates merges on test jobs, but the test step is an echo placeholder and the workflow may never have run. (2) It says he integrated the WebSocket link and standardized the API contract, but blame credits the backend and the event-contract doc to teammates. (3) It says mask and text dropout let one checkpoint serve four conditioning modes, but text conditioning is unfinished and the dual-dropout run failed.

Unconfirmed facts are held back until Alex confirms them: the GPA (an open to-do), the coursework list (inferred), Prof. Simeone vs. 'Daniel' Marino (the site uses Simeone, as on the resume and in git), whether the LinkedIn URL resolves, and the manuscript wording (only 'in preparation', never a title or author list).

Links stay off the page until fixed or approved. Inference-Server needs a real README, and HANDOFF.md removed from the public repo, before it is linked. Socr_2026 exposes the unpublished manuscript draft, so it needs lab approval first. The Hugging Face Space is not linked: the work is on an unmerged branch, visitors would spend GPU quota, and the generate endpoint is open. TTTDTT is private and its UI is never shown. Noverwatch has no repo, and the exe is never published.

Medical imagery: the brain must be an original procedural illustration, never BraTS slices or model outputs (they fall under a data-use agreement). It is labeled 'illustration: not model output, not patient data'. The lesion stays abstract, and Blip is never the tumor.
Trademark: Overwatch appears as text only (no logo, colors, typeface or art), and the window chrome is generic, not a Windows replica.

Low-end phones may struggle with SVG transform churn and the canvas. Mitigations: at most 350 nodes per stage, only the active stage updates, the canvas redraws only when t changes, offscreen loops pause, and the rail has a motion-off toggle. Verify at 4x CPU throttle.

concept.conceptName: Signal Path: a living schematic of Alex Liu
concept.pitch: The whole page is one engineering drawing, and the visitor's scroll is its clock. A single orange packet starts as the cursor after Alex's name and follows one continuous wire through each project, where it runs that project's real mechanism: it waits as a parked Future in a Redis queue, denoises from static into a brain slice over 200 steps, pings across telemetry sockets, and gets killed on launch by a Windows service. Recruiters remember it because each animation is the actual system, drawn accurately (real RPUSH/BLPOP ops, the real "8 jobs or 200 ms" batch rule, real byte counts), the attribution and the numbers are visibly honest, and the page tells exactly one joke, at the end, when the packet tries to play Overwatch.

Without scrolling, a recruiter already has the name, school, degree, graduation date, GPA, a one-line pitch, and visible proof of care.
narrative: COPY RULE (applies everywhere): every beat has two lines. The PLAIN line is Archivo 600, 20-24 px, short and declarative, first person, no adjectives, written so a non-engineer recruiter gets it. The SPEC line is JetBrains Mono 12 px and holds the exact mechanism (Redis op, tensor shape, byte layout) for engineers. Microcopy reads like a terse log. Caveat margin notes, at most 12 on the whole page, carry the honesty and the asides. No exclamation marks except inside Noverwatch's own quoted log strings.

DWG 00: POWER-ON (hero). The name and school appear as a part on the drawing (U1 with labeled pins). Tone: quiet confidence. The only joke is the NC pin ('offline LeetCode kit, for flights'). The packet starts as the text cursor.

NETLIST: a datasheet-style index, one row per project, generated from the data file: 'NET 01  inference-server  ->  request  /  Python, FastAPI, Redis'. Each row links to its drawing. Tone: a component datasheet.

DWG 01: INFERENCE SERVER, 'From POST to prediction.' The packet becomes a request, parks as a Future, waits in the Redis 'jobs' list, gets batched with 7 others, passes through ResNet-18 and comes home as 24 bytes. Tone: precise and a little proud of the plumbing. The margin note explains why there is no speedup number yet.

DWG 02: SOCR BRAINGEN, 'From static to scan.' The packet becomes Gaussian noise and denoises over 200 steps into an illustrative axial slice with a lesion placed by the atlas. Tone: careful researcher. It says 'illustration' out loud and credits labmates by role.

DWG 03: CLAWS, 'Telemetry for people in spacesuits.' The packet becomes a ping that fans out over Socket.IO, runs through Alex's caution-and-warning rules, then drops into the 5 Hz onboarding mock he built for new teammates. Tone: team player. Teammate-built blocks are drawn dashed and labeled as theirs.

DWG 04: NOVERWATCH, 'Self-defense.' The packet becomes Overwatch.exe, walks into a WMI tripwire and is killed. It respawns dazed. Tone: deadpan. This is the only full joke on the page, placed last among the projects so it is the aftertaste before the serious closing.

concept.character:
THE PACKET. It is a 10x10 px square with a 2 px radius, filled with --signal. In light mode it has a 1 px --ink keyline so it reads on paper; dark mode drops the keyline. A pseudo-element draws a 40 px radial halo (--halo fading to transparent) that breathes between scale 0.9 and 1.1 over 2.4 s. A 3-ghost trail (opacity .30/.16/.07) appears only while speed exceeds 4 px per frame.

RENDERING. It is ONE fixed-position div#packet (aria-hidden) moved only with translate3d (will-change: transform; contain: layout paint style). It sits at z-index 30, above content, and only the packet itself takes pointer events. Every costume is a child element of that same div, switched by its data-form attribute with a 160 ms scale and opacity morph. When a scene must take over drawing (the BrainGen noise canvas, the Noverwatch kill), the scene hides the packet at the exact screen point it starts drawing from and returns it at the exit port. The page therefore always has exactly one character.

COSTUMES:
- cursor: a 0.55em x 1em block that blinks (hero).
- packet: the default square.
- capsule: a 56x16 pill whose mono label reads 'POST /', then scrambles into the hex job_id.
- bytes: a strip of 16 or 24 cells, 3x6 px each. UUID cells are ink; payload cells are signal.
- noise: dissolves into the BrainGen canvas.
- ping: a dot plus two rings expanding from 0 to 22 px over 1.2 s.
- datagram: 8 cells.
- json: a '{...}' glyph.
- window: a 64x40 mini window titled 'Overwatch.exe', showing 'PID 12400' and a progress bar.
- flatline: a 2 px line.
- dazed: the square rotated 8 degrees, with one wobble.

BEHAVIOUR. Between drawings the packet rests on the bus at the read line (42% of viewport height), so the page scrolls under it like a wire under a probe. Moving dashes on the bus (dash offset tied to scrollY) show that it is travelling. Inside a drawing it follows the scene's path at that scene's progress. It chases its target with critically damped smoothing, so wheel steps never stutter.

REACTIONS. Hover shows its live state in mono, for example 'job_id 7f3a...c21e / queued / pos 3 of 8' or 't = 450 / step 110/200 / seed 48213'. A click makes it ping and logs 'packet: started as the cursor up top. long story.' After 8 s with no scroll it pings once, and the status line says 'still here. scroll to continue transmission.'

scenes.form: Request capsule, then a 16-byte job_id strip, then a 24-byte response strip ('<16sq'), then back to the packet.
scenes.scrollChoreography:
The sheet is a 720x600 viewBox.
- Left: a CLIENT block and a 'main.py: FastAPI on uvicorn :8001' block. Inside it are a pending_jobs table (rows of 'id -> Future') and a response_reader sub-box marked 'own connection r_reader'.
- Center: a Redis block with a KV drawer ('SET id bytes'), a horizontal 8-slot 'jobs' lane labeled 'FIFO: RPUSH tail / BLPOP head', and a 'response' lane.
- Right: 4 worker lanes, W1-W4, labeled 'N workers (4 in my benchmarks)'. Each lane has an 8-slot tray and a ResNet-18 glyph drawn as 18 thin ticks.

Beats, as pure functions of p:
- 0.00-0.06 TAP IN: the packet leaves the bus by a via on the left edge into CLIENT. Plain: 'A request comes in.' Spec: 'POST / / multipart image'.
- 0.06-0.14 NAME IT: the packet stretches into a capsule. Its label scrambles through 32 hex characters (crypto.getRandomValues, unique per visit) and settles on 'job_id 7f3a...c21e'. Spec: 'uuid.uuid4().bytes -> 16 B'.
- 0.14-0.22 PARK: a row draws into pending_jobs, '7f3a... -> Future', with a dashed ring rotating once every 6 s. The capsule splits: an image tile drops into the KV drawer ('SET 7f3a... <bytes>') while the 16-cell id strip, now the packet, continues. Plain: 'It parks. The server keeps serving.'
- 0.22-0.36 QUEUE: the strip enters the tail of 'jobs' ('RPUSH jobs'). Seven ghost ids in ink-3 arrive on a fixed stagger, so ours sits 3rd from the head. All four lanes show 'BLPOP jobs 1' on a 1 s blink. Plain: 'Only a 16-byte ID waits in line.'
- 0.36-0.52 BATCH: W2 pops the head and an 8-slot tray opens. A 200 ms deadline arc around the tray fills with p. Ids hop in one every 0.02 p ('BLPOP jobs 0.05'); ours lands in slot 3. At 8/8 the lid snaps shut with 'closed: full (8/8)'. Plain: 'Up to 8 jobs, or whatever arrived in 200 ms.'
- 0.52-0.62 FETCH: one bundled 8-strand line draws from KV to W2 ('MGET id1..id8'), then the KV rows strike through ('DEL id1..id8'). Plain: 'One round trip for all eight images.'
- 0.62-0.76 INFER: the slots stack into an isometric block '[8,3,224,224]'. The 18 ResNet ticks light left to right with p. The output appears as '[8,1000]', drawn as 8 tiny sparkline rows; each row's argmax dot pops, and ours glows. Spec: 'torch.no_grad / CPU / torch.set_num_threads(1)'. Plain: 'One forward pass for the whole batch.'
- 0.76-0.86 PACK: the packet becomes a 24-cell strip (16 ink cells, 8 signal cells) labeled 'struct.pack("<16sq") -> 24 B'. It travels 'RPUSH response'. Plain: 'The answer goes home as 24 bytes, not JSON.'
- 0.86-0.94 WAKE: response_reader runs 'BLPOP response 1' and unpacks. The pending_jobs ring fills solid (set_result). Plain: 'One reader wakes exactly the right request.'
- 0.94-1.00 RETURN: CLIENT types '{"Category_Number": 281, "Server_Rate": <seconds>}', tagged 'example', then '200 OK'. The packet re-forms as a square and exits by the lower-left via to the bus.

Scrolling up reverses every beat exactly.
scenes.clickHoverReactions:
- CLIENT is a real button, 'send request' (Enter or Space also works). Each press starts a live ghost request in a small client-side simulation of the real policy, shown at 1/10 speed under a '×0.1 time' label. The request runs RPUSH; the first idle worker of the four does BLPOP; the tray opens and closes at 8 jobs or after 200 ms of sim time (2 s real). Clicking 8 or more times inside the window gives 'full (8/8)'; otherwise you get 'deadline (k/8)'. A tally under CLIENT reads 'you: n sent / batches: a full, b deadline'. This layer never disturbs the scroll-scrubbed state.
- Hover or focus a Redis op label for its exact meaning: 'RPUSH jobs <id>: append to tail', 'BLPOP jobs 1: block up to 1 s, then loop', 'MGET / DEL: one round trip each', 'SET <id> <bytes>: payload stays in Redis; only the id is queued'.
- Hover a worker lane: 'worker.py / 1 torch thread / CPU'.
- Hover response_reader to reveal 'replay the bug' (always visible on touch). It plays for 3 s:
  - An idle clock counts to 5 s.
  - The wire between Redis and the reader snaps open with a 2-frame spark.
  - The reader box is struck through: 'task died silently: redis-py 8 default socket timeout 5 s, unbounded BLPOP'.
  - New Futures pile up hollow.
  - The gap re-solders (stroke reveal): 'fix: bounded BLPOP response 1 + done-callback that prints the exception'.
- Hover the packet: 'job_id 7f3a...c21e / queued / pos 3 of 8'.
scenes.contentLayout:
Desktop: a grid of text (5/12), the bus lane (64 px), then the stage (7/12). The stage is sticky at top 8vh with height 84vh. Its title block reads 'DWG 01 / INFERENCE SERVER / REV b10d04f / JUN-SEP 2026 / PERSONAL PROJECT'. The text column has:
- kicker 'DWG 01 / personal project, 2026'
- h2 'Inference Server' and the tagline
- the lede: 'A model server I built from scratch to learn what happens between POST and prediction.'
- five steps, each min-height 56vh:
  1. 'Park, don't poll.' (Future under a 16-byte UUID; one reader task)
  2. 'Only bytes cross the boundary.' (SET + RPUSH; inference never runs on the event loop)
  3. 'Eight, or 200 ms.' (MGET/DEL, one stacked pass)
  4. 'The bug that only happened when nothing happened.' (5 s socket timeout, bounded BLPOP, done-callback)
  5. 'I wrote the load generator too.' (asyncio + httpx, 10 to 1,200 concurrent per level, p25-p95, failures grouped by status code; raised the read timeout to 30 s after spotting survivorship bias)
- a margin note by step 5: 'no speedup number on purpose: the same unbatched code measured ~2x apart on different days. rerunning it controlled first.'
- stack chips: Python, FastAPI, asyncio, Redis, PyTorch, ResNet-18
- the link 'source on GitHub', enabled after the README fix

Phone: the stage is sticky at top 0 with height 52svh and uses the tall viewBox 360x440: client and frontend on top, the Redis jobs lane in the middle, 4 compact worker rows at the bottom, and the response path up the right edge. Captions overlay the bottom of the stage; the steps scroll beneath it.

concept.genericScene:
GENERIC PIPELINE SCENE. It is used whenever an article's data-scene is missing or unknown, and also as the fallback if a custom scene throws during init.

INPUT
- The article's ol.flow: 3-7 li items. Each li's text is a short plain label. Optional data-kind is one of io|queue|compute|store|net. Optional data-op is a mono spec string. An optional title attribute holds a longer note.
- data-form picks the packet costume: packet|bytes|ping|json|window. The default is packet.
- data-rev and data-dates fill the title block.

LAYOUT
- Nodes go on a serpentine grid inside the standard 720x600 sheet. On desktop that is 2 rows of up to 4: the first row left to right, the second right to left. On phone it is a single column.
- Each node is a 150x64 box with:
  - a reference designator, auto-numbered by kind: J for io, Q for queue, U for compute, D for store, A for net (J1, U2, ...);
  - a 24 px symbol by kind: io is a port arrow into the box; queue is 4 stacked slots; compute is an IC with 3 pin stubs a side; store is a cylinder outline; net is two concentric arcs;
  - the label in Archivo 15 px and data-op in mono 11 px.
- The wire is one orthogonal route with 45-degree chamfers through every node's ports. Entry and exit vias sit on the sheet's left edge so it joins the bus like every other drawing.
- The title block (DWG number from order, name, REV, dates) and the zone markers are automatic.

CHOREOGRAPHY
- 0.00-0.06 is the tap in and 0.94-1.00 the tap out. The middle is split evenly into N segments.
- Within segment i:
  - the first 40%: the wire ahead draws (dashoffset);
  - 40-60%: node i's outline draws and its designator lights in signal;
  - 60-100%: the label types in (characters revealed by p), the packet sits in the node pulsing once, and a scene log strip at the bottom of the sheet appends '[i/N] <label> / <data-op>'.
- The caption pair is the label (plain) plus data-op (spec).

REACTIONS
- Hover or focus a node: it highlights and a callout shows its title note.
- Click a node: that segment replays over 600 ms (time-based) and the log prints 'replay: <label>'.
- Hover the packet: 'stage i/N: <label>'.

DEGRADATION
- No ol.flow: the h3s of ol.steps become the nodes.
- Neither list: one 'U1 <project name>' IC with the tagline as its part number. That is still a correct, good-looking drawing.
- Reduced motion: everything is drawn, and a static packet glyph sits on the last node.

Example data-only entry: Distributed MapReduce, with flow input -> partition -> map (6 workers) -> shuffle -> reduce -> output, an op 'heartbeats + task reassignment' on the manager node, and no link.
concept.visualSystem:
PALETTE. CSS custom properties live on :root. Dark mode is defined under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) guarded by :root:not([data-theme=light]), and again under :root[data-theme=dark]. body has an explicit background: var(--bg).

LIGHT, 'drafting paper':
- --bg #F3F0E8; --bg-raised #FBF9F4 (sheets)
- --grid-minor #14202E0D; --grid-major #14202E1A
- --ink #14202E (navy-black, a quiet nod to Michigan blue); --ink-2 #46515E; --ink-3 #626B76 (smallest text, 4.7:1 on bg)
- --ghost #A9B0B7 (teammate, context and inactive blocks; non-text only)
- --wire #14202E; --wire-idle #14202E40
- --signal #E5480B (packet and live traces; graphics only); --signal-text #B33A06 (orange text and annotations, 5.2:1); --halo #E5480B38
- --marker #FFD84D (highlighter, mix-blend multiply at 60%)
- --ok #2B7A4B; --warn #9A5B00; --danger #C2253A (all at least 4.6:1)
- --viewer #0B0E12 and --viewer-ink #D9DEE5 (the MRI viewer stays dark in both themes)

DARK, 'lab after hours':
- --bg #0C1117; --bg-raised #111821
- --grid-minor #8FB3D90D; --grid-major #8FB3D91C
- --ink #E8E4DA; --ink-2 #B4BAC2; --ink-3 #8C949E (6.2:1)
- --ghost #46515C
- --wire #E8E4DA; --wire-idle #E8E4DA33
- --signal #FF6A2B; --signal-text #FF8A57; --halo #FF6A2B55
- --marker #FFCB05 (Michigan maize: 22% alpha as label backing, full strength for 1 px underlines)
- --ok #4CC38A; --warn #F2B544; --danger #FF5A6E
- --viewer #05070A

Color rules:
- There is exactly one accent: signal.
- Maize appears only as the highlighter.
- Status colors appear only in CLAWS alerts and the Noverwatch kill stamp.
- No gradients anywhere except the packet halo. No purple, no glass, no drop shadows.
- Alerts always carry the words DANGER, WARN or FAST, never color alone.

TYPE. Google Fonts, one request, display=swap: Archivo:wdth,wght@62..125,400..800 + JetBrains Mono:wght@400;600 + Caveat:wght@500.
- h1 'Alex Liu': Archivo wdth 125, wght 780, clamp(48px, 11vw, 168px), tracking -0.025em, line-height 0.9.
- h2: wdth 112, wght 700, clamp(32px, 4.2vw, 56px). Its underline draws in as a dimension line with end ticks.
- Plain captions: wdth 100, wght 600, 20-24 px.
- Body: wdth 100, wght 400, 17px/1.6 (16 px on phone), max 62ch.
- JetBrains Mono for every label, designator, Redis op, log line and title block: 11-13 px, tabular-nums. Designators and labels are uppercase with 0.06em tracking; logs are sentence case.
- Caveat 500 only for margin notes (12 or fewer): 20 px in --signal-text, rotated -1.5 degrees, each paired with a hand-drawn SVG arrow.

SPACE
- 4 px base. Tokens: 4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64/96/128.
- Paper grid: 8 px minor, 40 px major.
- Container max 1320 px. Desktop columns: text 5/12, a 64 px bus lane, stage 7/12. Stages are sticky at top 8vh, height 84vh.
- Phone: 16 px side gutter, bus at x=12 px, content indented 28 px.

TEXTURE. No noise and no images; the texture comes from drafting conventions.
- The paper grid is two CSS linear-gradients with background-attachment: scroll.
- Every stage is a sheet: a 1 px ink border, + registration marks in the corners, zone markers (A-D across the top, 1-4 down the left) in 10 px mono ink-3, and a title block bottom-right (DWG / TITLE / REV / DATE / SHEET).
- Wires are 1.5 px with vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke and 10-unit 45-degree chamfers.
- Vias at taps are 3 px with a 1 px hole. Junction dots at fan-outs are 4 px.
- Context and teammate blocks are dashed (4 3) in --ghost. Alex's blocks are solid ink with a marker band behind the label.
- Net flags on the bus (a tag shape: 'NET 02 -> socr-braingen') act as wayfinding.

MOTION
- Scroll-scrubbed beats are linear in p, because the scroll is the clock, and fully reversible.
- The packet chases its target with critically damped smoothing, k = 1 - e^(-14·dt).
- Time-based UI uses --ease-out cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) at 240 ms.
- Line draws use --ease-draw cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) at 600-800 ms.
- Highlighter swipe: 240 ms ease-out. Caption crossfade: 180 ms. Costume morph: 160 ms.
- The Noverwatch kill uses cubic-bezier(.7,0,1,.3) at 120 ms: accelerating and deliberately abrupt.
- Cursor blink: steps(1), 1.06 s. Halo breath: 2.4 s ease-in-out, alternate.
- Only transform, opacity and stroke-dashoffset ever animate.
