RENDERING
- All words are DOM text.
- Each stage is an inline SVG generated by JS from primitives in app.js:
  - box(x,y,w,h,label,ref,kind)
  - route(points): an orthogonal path with 10-unit chamfers
  - via, junction, tray(n), bytes(n), plate, label, caption
  Every path gets pathLength=1, so a reveal is just stroke-dasharray 1 with stroke-dashoffset 1 - t, and no getTotalLength calls are needed. vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke keeps 1.5 px lines crisp at any scale. Colors come from currentColor and CSS vars, so theming costs nothing.
- Canvases appear only in BrainGen: the 160x160 viewer and the 64x64 mask plate. x0 and eps are precomputed Float32Arrays from a seeded mulberry32. Each frame does one putImageData of about 25.6k pixels (under 0.5 ms).
- The bus is pure CSS: a dashed full-height line, plus a solid line scaled with transform: scaleY to the packet's furthest progress.
- The packet is one fixed div.

SCROLL MECHANISM
- Stages use position: sticky inside each article. The text column's natural height is the scroll runway; steps get a min-height of 56vh (60svh on phone).
- measure() runs on load, after document.fonts.ready, and on a ResizeObserver on documentElement, debounced 120 ms. On phones, height-only changes under 120 px are ignored so the iOS address bar doesn't trigger re-measures. It caches, per article: top, height, sticky offset, the stage rect and viewBox scale. It also caches the hero route as a lookup table, sampling getPointAtLength once every 4 units into a Float32Array.
- A passive scroll listener only marks the page dirty and requests a frame.
- Each frame reads scrollY once. For each article, p = clamp((y + stickyTop - top) / (height - stageH), 0, 1). An IntersectionObserver with a 50% rootMargin decides which scenes are live.
- A scene's update(p) runs only when |dp| > 0.0005 or one of its sims is active. The beats engine calls each beat as run(clamp((p - a)/(b - a))). Every visual is therefore a pure function of p: reversible, and correct after anchor or j/k jumps (p >= 1 renders the finished state).
- Packet target: the active scene's packetAt(p), converted from stage coordinates to the screen with the cached rect; otherwise the bus point at 42% of viewport height. Smoothing uses k = 1 - e^(-14·dt). The trail lags at 0.6/0.4/0.25 of k.
- Click demos (batch sim, gauge spikes, PLAY, mask regrow, seed replay) run on a tiny timer queue inside the same loop, in their own SVG layer.
- The loop cancels itself when the packet has settled (under 0.1 px) and no sims are running, so an idle page uses zero CPU.
- The status log writes only when a beat changes.
- Every scene init is wrapped in try/catch: a failure falls back to the generic scene, and a generic failure falls back to the no-JS schematic.

PERF BUDGET
- Sizes: HTML ≤ 45 KB, CSS ≤ 24 KB, JS ≤ 60 KB raw (about 18 KB gzip), fonts ≤ 160 KB woff2 (latin subsets), og.png ≤ 120 KB (not loaded by the page).
- Runtime: per-frame JS ≤ 3 ms on a mid laptop (integrated GPU). No layout reads inside the loop, no SVG filters, no animated shadows or blur. Only transform, opacity and stroke-dashoffset change. Canvas DPR is clamped to 2 (1 on phones).
- Targets: Lighthouse performance ≥ 95, accessibility 100, CLS 0 (stage sizes reserved in CSS), LCP is the h1 text at under 1.2 s on desktop.
- ?selftest runs console.assert checks: the batch sim closes at 8 jobs or 200 ms; mask area lands inside its size bin; p is monotonic and clamped across sections.

REDUCED MOTION
- matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') adds html.rm, and the change event is handled live.
- No scroll-scrubbing: each scene renders still(), a composed final state with all strokes drawn.
- The fixed packet is hidden; each sheet shows a static packet glyph at its signature spot:
  - Inference: the 24-byte strip on the response lane.
  - BrainGen: a 5-frame filmstrip at t = 995/750/500/250/0 in place of the live canvas.
  - CLAWS: one WARN and one DANGER alert.
  - Noverwatch: the flatlined window beside its log lines.
- The cursor is solid, there is no 5 Hz pulse and no trail. Interactions still work, but state changes happen instantly with no tween. Sticky positioning stays (it is not motion).

NO-JS
- html.no-js hides the stages, netlist, theme switch and packet.
- ol.flow renders as a CSS vertical schematic: numbered bordered boxes joined by ::before connector lines, with data-op shown via attr() in mono. The bus line and grid are pure CSS, so the wire still threads the page.
- Changelog details/summary works natively. The theme follows prefers-color-scheme in CSS.
- A header nav of plain anchors covers navigation.

ACCESSIBILITY
- Skip link. Stage SVGs are aria-hidden; the article text is their equivalent.
- Every control is a real button, radio or input with a label, visible 2 px signal focus, and a 44 px minimum touch target.
- Tooltips open on hover AND focus. The status log is aria-hidden (decorative).
- All tokens meet AA contrast.

MOBILE (≤ 760 px)
- Single column. The bus sits at x=12 px, and each sticky stage spans from 24 px to the right gutter, so its tap still meets the bus.
- Stages are sticky at top 0 with height 52-56svh (svh units, never vh). Scenes ship a 'tall' layout table (viewBox 360x440). Captions overlay the bottom of the stage, and text steps scroll underneath it on an opaque background.
- Hover becomes tap: the first tap reveals, the second acts. The BrainGen crosshair works on tap only.
- Trail drops to 1 ghost. The status bar is one line at the bottom, padded with safe-area-inset-bottom.
- Hero U1 becomes a vertical pin list.

1. Static content and CSS until the no-JS page is complete and handsome.
2. Bus, packet and hero route.
3. Beats engine, primitives and the generic scene.
4. Custom scenes, in order: Noverwatch, Inference, CLAWS, BrainGen.
5. Reduced-motion and phone pass.
